# Oxide Launcher 1.6.0

Every screen is the Oxide GUI now, including the ones inside the game window. The launcher used to
crash on its own front page on most landscape phones. Discover pages, dependencies are visible and
selectable, and installing opens a menu instead of starting immediately.

## The launcher crashed on its front page

    IllegalStateException: Vertically scrollable component was measured with an
    infinity maximum height constraints, which is disallowed.

`verticalScroll` measures its content with an infinite maximum height. The Home environment card
had a `verticalScroll` inside the compact page's own `verticalScroll`, and nothing in between
clamped it, so the inner one threw during measure and the activity went down.

Home picks the compact layout at 900dp wide or less, which on a landscape phone is most hardware -
1920x1080 at 420dpi and 2560x1440 at 560dpi both land on 731dp. So this was the first screen on the
majority of devices. It survived release testing only because the card shows a loading row until
the environment probe returns, and the crash needs real rows to measure.

The inner scroll is gone; the compact page column already scrolls, so those rows belong in it. The
exception is not caught anywhere - the constraint source is what changed.

## Every remaining route into the old interface is closed

Settings reached the old Zalith host through a single function. Selecting Java, Renderer, Controls,
Gamepad or About handed that function a nested navigation key, which pushed the original settings
screen - old icon top bar, pink accent rail and all - over the new one. All eight sections now
resolve to an Oxide panel, to a row the Settings page already owns, or to nothing. The old stack
cannot be reached from the new GUI.

Control layouts got a real panel: select, copy, import, create, delete with confirmation, share, and
open in the editor. Controls and Gamepad are a new inline panel covering mouse, all eight pointer
hotspots, gestures, gyroscope, gamepad, and a binding drawer over every GamepadMap row. The
pointer hotspots had no row at all before.

## Launch no longer falls back to dialogs

The Oxide launch page was shown only once a launch flow existed, which is after the game starts.
The whole pre-flight chain - including a suspending Vulkan check - ran before that, hosted by the
activity as seven legacy dialogs. So pressing Play on an unsupported renderer, an expired Microsoft
token, a missing game version name or an ungranted storage permission dropped you into the old
look. The launch page now covers the pre-flight window too, and all seven are inline rows with the
backend carried over unchanged.

Choosing "authorize" now continues the launch. It used to request the permission and then abandon
the launch regardless of the outcome, so granting it did nothing and you had to press Play again
with no message.

## Discover actually pages

It stopped after about twenty results. It now accumulates a feed: it loads the next page eight items
from the end, de-duplicates across pages so a shifting result set cannot show a project twice, and
cancels in-flight work whenever you change the provider, category, search, game version or loader, so
a slow response cannot land in a list you have already changed. Page size and index respect the
server's caps rather than requesting a page it will reject.

A failure partway through renders the results it already has, plus an error row and a retry for that
page. Previously a swallowed failure was indistinguishable from "no results", which is exactly why
CurseForge looked broken for so long.

## Dependencies are visible before anything downloads

Tapping install now opens a menu first. It shows the project's dependencies with their real type and
the version that matches the game version you picked, lets you select which ones you want, and
auto-detects the Minecraft version from your current instance while still letting you choose another.
If that version is not installed, it offers to install it with the project and asks you to confirm.
This applies to mods and modpacks; shaders, resource packs, saves and maps install directly as
before.

"Download all" submits one task per selected dependency, so one failure cannot silently drop the
rest, and each dependency carries its own error and its own retry. CurseForge dependencies also
resolve to the exact file the mod author pinned. They used to resolve to the newest version that
happened to match your game version, which is often the wrong one.

## The in-game menu

The last surface still wearing the old design: a five-tab Material pager in two columns where every
slider opened a legacy edit dialog. It is one dismissible panel with a section rail, sized from the
measured window so it works at tiny resolutions. All 14 switches, 17 sliders, 8 pickers and 8 action
rows are still there. Slider values are edited inline instead of in a dialog, and rotating while the
menu is open no longer leaves the resolution clamp calculated against the old screen size.

## The icon was a reconstruction of the artwork, not the artwork

The shipped icon was white and orange rotated squares. Those were generated by measuring the artwork
as if the logo sat on a flat background, keeping only the faint glow edges, and fitting two nested
rounded squares to them - the metal, the orange material and the ring were all discarded before
anything was drawn. Every raster is now cut from the artwork itself, across all five densities,
including the adaptive foreground and the monochrome layer, which had been left describing the old
squares. The in-app mark was a rotated square too; it is now the same octagonal ring as the icon.

## Version

This is release v1.6.0. The launcher reports itself as **1.0.0** in About, in the sidebar footer, on
the Home screen and in crash reports. That is deliberate: the release identity and the product
version are different facts. The update check, the HTTP user agent, the JVM launcher-version argument
and the modpack metadata template all keep the build version, because other software compares against
them and they have to move monotonically.

## Verified

Compilation, unit tests, lint, R8, packaging and signing, through CI. Not validated on physical
hardware - that is what this release is for.
